chapter: Playing New Orleans and the coast
title: Sam at the Estory Garden, Jim Robinson, and Howard versus Alvin
summary: Sam's rehearsal-free hard numbers, Jim Robinson's playing, and the trumpeters Howard and Alvin in George Lewis's band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: And because my brother Sam, he read when he was up here, I don't know what he did in the country, see. Me and Sam used to put them old hard numbers on us up there on the Estory Garden, I heard Al speaking about the Estory. He bring them numbers right there and let that place get full of people and then he'd draw them out there. Put them up there. But you hadn't rehearsed even? No, he said, who fall down, stay down. See I can't get you all to rehearse. Miss Trombone, Sally Trombone, all that's for trombone work. Well you see they didn't have Jim Hook because Jim had done played them numbers with Chris Kelly. You see? And he's a good year man already, and he's slick. And he had everything his way. And he said, now he'd bring them numbers, now I think he can catch me. But see I was playing first trumpet, you see? And the trombone part, all Jim wanted to do, the other corner leading, and he could harmonize some kind of way, and he hardly would go wrong. You see? Well that's the thing that saved him. Now I don't know why they, now Howard is another one. He's been playing a whole lot of stuff for Jim. And he didn't, don't worry Jim. I think that's why they turned that other boy off. Alvin, Alvin was a better musician in Howard, and he got better lips in Howard.

And I don't see why they turned that way. And I don't see why they turned anymore. I think he couldn't travel or something. Maybe I think he had a job here and they went on the road. Alvin didn't want to go on the road or something.

Because Jim, Jim is, and Howard is friends. And then they had them fired Howard. And I don't know why they had taken him back. And I could never get in touch with George and Lewis. I could never get that boy's phone number. I asked Jim his phone number. He told me, look in the phone book.
But there's so many of them. It's the one on DeArmond Street.
I have the number. I can give it to you after a while.
